what_this_is: the first time a browser has drawn this publication, and the browser half of queue item 3. s3-10 measured in Python where the page WOULD draw the raster and wrote eleven probes with their expected answers before any browser ran. This is that oracle read back off a live page: the cell the card names, the cell the picture paints, the colour of both, and the words a household gets on hover.

where.page: http://localhost:8099/ serving v2/spikes/g3-render from the working tree
where.threshold: the page default, 20 minutes, on the single published layer

how_to_reproduce: append <script src='probe_placement.js'> to the page (NOT eval: the file is strict-mode so eval keeps the function in its own scope)
fetch the oracle and call g3RunPlacementProbe(oracle, { hover: true })
the run takes under nine seconds and touches nothing: G3Probe cannot set a threshold, enable a layer, move the map or render a card

the_first_run_found_two_defects_in_the_i.what_happened: the first run reported 14 disagreements with the oracle. Every one of them was in the instrument. The GEOMETRY agreed at all eleven probes on that first run, including the three sensitive ones, and nothing about the geometry was changed afterwards.

defect_1_translucent_colour_cannot_be_re.symptom: the page's blue read back (24,119,241,150) where the oracle said (24,119,242,150), and its hatch grey (61,61,61,130) where the oracle said (60,60,60,130)
defect_1_translucent_colour_cannot_be_re.cause: a canvas stores a translucent pixel premultiplied by alpha in eight bits, so getImageData cannot return the byte that was written
defect_1_translucent_colour_cannot_be_re.control_run_in_the_same_call: two OPAQUE pixels written and read in the same canvas came back exactly, which is what makes this premultiplication rather than a painting error
defect_1_translucent_colour_cannot_be_re.fix: colour is compared to within one count per channel and alpha exactly; alpha is what separates included (150) from nodata (130) from excluded (0), so nothing a household reads as in or out rests on the tolerance
defect_1_translucent_colour_cannot_be_re.proof_the_tolerance_did_not_blind_it: a new self-test check shifts a channel by three counts and requires it to be caught

defect_2_the_pointer_cannot_be_put_on_a_.symptom: the hover read a card for the cell one column west, or one row north, of the probe: '(row 100, col 72)' for a probe about (100, 73), '(row 200, col 124)' for a probe about (201, 124), and 'outside the published area' at two corners
defect_2_the_pointer_cannot_be_put_on_a_.cause: MouseEvent's clientX/clientY are IDL `long`, so a fractional value is truncated when the event is constructed. Measured: 464.378 arrives as 464
defect_2_the_pointer_cannot_be_put_on_a_.why_it_mattered_here: at the whole-footprint view one screen pixel is 0.671 of a row, so losing up to a pixel moves the reading up to two thirds of a cell -- and every probe worth having sits on a cell boundary
defect_2_the_pointer_cannot_be_put_on_a_.fix: the whole pixel is now chosen deliberately: the nearest one whose own coordinates resolve to the cell the probe is about. If no pixel in the neighbourhood does, the probe records that rather than reading a card for somewhere else

the_first_run_found_two_defects_in_the_i.the_lesson: the Node self-test had stubbed away both behaviours -- its MouseEvent kept fractional coordinates and its maskPixel returned the bytes that were written -- so it proved the instrument could fail at the error I had modelled and said nothing about the two it stood in for. The self-test now reproduces both exactly and is at least as hostile as Chrome.

the_run.what_zero_disagreements_would_mean: that the page places the raster exactly as measure_drawn_pixel.py predicts, including the sub-row displacement, so the structure counts in that artifact describe the page a household actually gets
the_run.what_this_cannot_see: an AFFINE placement error. The drawn row is recovered from where the quad's own corners project, so a constant offset or a uniform stretch of the texture cancels out and this probe reports agreement. Only the SHAPE of the placement is visible to it, which is the Mercator-against-latitude question it was built for. Closing the rest needs a rendered pixel: a screenshot at a colour edge, checked against the screen row predicted from corner_screen_y and drawn_rows_per_screen_pixel above.

the_affine_check_the_probe_declares_it_c.why_it_is_needed: the probe recovers the drawn row from where the quad's own corners project, so a constant offset or a uniform stretch of the texture cancels and it reports agreement. probe_placement_selftest.mjs asserts that blindness with a page placed a whole row off, and the probe declares it in its own output. Closing it needs a RENDERED pixel.
the_affine_check_the_probe_declares_it_c.method: zoom in until one raster row is 38 screen pixels, find the row boundary with the most colour transitions in view (row 105/106, eleven columns in three runs), and draw four one-pixel lines across exactly those columns: where MapLibre's quad places the boundary, where the publication places it (linear in latitude), and the same boundary plus and minus one whole row. Then photograph it.
the_affine_check_the_probe_declares_it_c.result: the painted edge sits on the Mercator line. The latitude line is 9 px south of it, inside ground the page has left unpainted, and the plus and minus one row controls are 38 px away on either side. So the texture is drawn where its corners project, to well inside a row, and the sub-row displacement s3-10 computed is visible in rendered pixels rather than inferred from a projection.
the_affine_check_the_probe_declares_it_c.what_is_still_judged_by_eye: the coincidence of the painted edge with the red line is read off an image, not computed: neither virtual environment here has an image library, and a canvas-source page cannot hand back its own rendered pixels. The competing hypotheses are drawn on the same image at 38 px separation, so the reading is coarse but the margin is large. A numeric version would decode the screenshot and fit the edge. CORRECTED 2026-11-16, Codex pass 55: the separation that matters is the 9.08 px between the Mercator and latitude hypotheses, NOT the 38 px controls. The one-row controls show only that a gross whole-row alternative would be conspicuous; they do not establish precision sufficient to resolve 9 px. The image does supply that narrower discrimination reasonably well, and a one-pixel overlay partly obscures the very edge being judged. The defensible conclusion is local visual consistency at one edge, not closure of every affine placement error. Also corrected: the column spans listed here cover EIGHT columns, not eleven.

what_this_establishes: at eleven coordinates the live map's projection and the SOURCE CANVAS samples agreed with measure_drawn_pixel.py's analytical expectations, including the sub-row displacement -- twice, on 2026-11-15 and again on 2026-11-16 against the corrected oracle. CORRECTED 2026-11-16, Codex pass 55 F3: this said 'the page draws the published raster where measure_drawn_pixel.py predicted'. The probe reads the canvas the page hands MapLibre and computes the drawn row from the quad's projected corners; it never samples a rendered map pixel, so it cannot by itself confirm what was painted. The screenshot at one colour edge carries that part, locally and by eye

the structure counts in s3-10 remain ANALYTICAL counts under the placement model, now supported locally by an image at one colour edge: at the 20 minutes the page opens on, 5,801 structures stand where the painted colour would contradict their own card, 2,771 of them painted outside the coloured area although the publication includes them. CORRECTED 2026-11-16, F3: this said the counts 'describe the page a household actually gets'. Eleven probes and one edge do not promote an analytical count into an observed exposure. See also F8: the 5,801 counts OUTCOME disagreement, not colour disagreement
all three sensitive probes showed the contradiction in the live page: the card named one cell while the pixel under the pointer was painted from the next row down

the three disclosures a household is owed were rendered in a browser for the first time, in one card: the cell identity (row 100, col 73), the restricted-route warning, and 'measured to one of 2 places at this junction: Weaver Street Market, Inc, Weaver Street Market Administration'
what_this_does_not_establish: anything about a phone: this is one desktop Chrome at devicePixelRatio 1

anything about the model underneath. The probe compares the page against the publication, not the publication against the ground. The one walked route in the record is an owner report of about 25 minutes against a published 14, and it is not admissible: not stopwatch-timed, no start door recorded, no destination pinned. CORRECTED 2026-11-16, pass 55: this said the walked route 'disagrees with the model by 20 minutes', which is neither figure, and no admissible difference has been established

that 36 m is acceptable. It is now measured, confirmed in a browser and visible in a picture; whether to fix it by regridding in Mercator, by placing the quad per row, or not at all, is the owner's call

that the card's opening sentence is right. 'Every criterion you have on is satisfied here' is what the page said on this run, and what card-at-boundary-north.jpg shows; pass 54 asked for 'the model estimates this cell meets your limits'.
